slot.brief: Predict the products when an unsymmetrical ether reacts with excess HI, highlighting the SN1 vs SN2 pathway depending on the alkyl groups.

stem: When tert-butyl methyl ether is heated with excess HI, what are the major organic products?

verdicts.working: HI cleaves the ether at the tertiary carbon to form tert-butyl iodide and methanol. Excess HI converts methanol to methyl iodide, so the products are tert-butyl iodide and methyl iodide.

working:
Protonated ether cleaves at the tertiary carbon by $\text{S}_\text{N}1$: tert-butyl iodide + methanol.\nExcess HI converts methanol to methyl iodide.\nMajor organic products: tert-butyl iodide and methyl iodide.

Independent check: HI cleaves the ether at the tertiary carbon to form tert-butyl iodide and methanol. Excess HI converts methanol to methyl iodide, so the products are tert-butyl iodide and methyl iodide.
solution:
The protonated ether cleaves at the tertiary carbon by an $\mathrm{S_N1}$ pathway, forming tert-butyl iodide and methanol. Excess HI converts the methanol into methyl iodide:
$$\text{tert-butyl methyl ether} + 2\mathrm{HI} \longrightarrow \text{tert-butyl iodide} + \text{methyl iodide} + \mathrm{H_2O}$$
Thus, the major organic products are tert-butyl iodide and methyl iodide.
